what_happened: Dispatch's measured population numbers (8 require_file users, 88 scripts/lib referencers, 3 historical repairs) were independently re-measured against the live tree and corroborated almost exactly (90 vs 88, within noise of 2 intervening commits); all three historical repair commits (d3e45535e, 1c10b01f7, 4c96ccb4f) were confirmed via git show against pre-repair text, giving the research report's detector design a verified historical ground truth rather than a speculative one.

Dispatch's Shape-1 enumeration ('Three suites declare one today') undercounts the true named-array population: 8 suites (not 3) declare a REQUIRED_LIBS/REQUIRED_SCRIPTS/REQUIRED_LIB_SCRIPTS/REQUIRED_CORE_SCRIPTS-family array consumed by both a require/existence loop and a cp-into-sandbox loop, and at least 7 more declare the open-coded parallel-pair shape. The dispatch's own text anticipated this risk explicitly ('do not assume the array-declaring three are the population'), so this is recorded as a stale-enumeration note for the plan/implement phases to size the suite-selection predicate against the wider measured set, not a correction of the dispatch's reasoning.

Research report recommended creating two new source-store scripts (the lint and its regression suite) but did not identify that core/manifest.json's provides.scripts is an explicit 409-entry non-glob list whose completeness is enforced by check-extension-docs.sh Rule Q inside verify-deploy.sh gate 3 (commit-blocking). Plan adds the manifest.json declaration plus sync-manifest-scripts.sh regeneration to each script-creating phase per plan-format.md's coupled-generated-surface obligation.

class: tooling caught an authoring defect early
what_happened: validate-artifact.sh's Tier Justification measurement check caught two genuinely wrong claims at plan-authoring time: suite_selection_select returns __FULL_SWEEP__ for a path SET when ANY member is unmappable (so naming test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh for a phase that also creates a new .sh was a fabricated coverage claim), and the check requires the claimed suite list to EXACTLY equal the selector output, not merely be drawn from it. Both corrected before the plan was returned; final validation is 0 warnings.

sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write reported 0 missing for a brand-new lint script until it was 'git add'-ed first -- it diffs against git ls-files, not a raw disk walk, so an untracked new script is invisible to it.

The plan's shape-iii default ('neither exit nor passing-through found -> MANDATORY, safe default') was wrong against the live corpus: update-phase-status.sh's bare 'if [[ -n "$hb_lib" ]]; then . "$hb_lib"; fi' with no error branch at all defaults to that same ambiguous case, and is genuinely OPTIONAL (degrade-safe). Flipped the default to OPTIONAL, matching the plan's OWN stated rule for shape iii ('a log-and-continue with no exit -> OPTIONAL') more literally than the plan's own prose summary of it.

class: detector false positive found by own regression suite
what_happened: Writing the Phase 2 dedicated OPTIONAL shape-iii negative case (update-task-status.sh) surfaced a real bug in Phase 1's detector: the shape-iii body-scan loop did not skip comment lines, so update-task-status.sh's own prose comment on the OVERLAP_LIB guard ('...which returns exit 1 at heredoc EOF...') was textually misread as the branch's own hard-fail exit signal, misclassifying file-scope-overlap.sh as MANDATORY. Fixed by adding a comment-skip to that loop. The live-corpus clean run never caught this because every suite in the real corpus that copies update-task-status.sh also happens to declare file-scope-overlap.sh anyway (for an unrelated reason), so the bug was latent until a dedicated isolation case exercised it.
